summary: DAWDLE DISCRIMINATION PROBE (ckpt5 lens, CPU, one-ply): 64 squander positions (8 ep9 marathons x 8 plies, archived corpus scripts/archive/_wf_r4_hd_positions.json, leader |v|>0.6 & leader to move) + 15 conversion controls (12 ep5 median games, last-30-ply, winner to move, v_win>0.6) + 24 ungated midgame controls (12 disjoint ep5 games, plies 40/60). At each position: top-12 prior moves + the played move, each applied and the successor evaluated with the SAME ckpt5 full forward (v 65-bin decode; moves_left 65-bin decode onto [0,512]). U_k = v(s') - k*sign(v_base)*ml(s')/512 for k in {0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0}; per-position exact critical-k also computed. FINDINGS: (Q1 grip) at squander points successor-v is FLAT — median best-to-2nd gap 0.0021, full candidate v-range 0.025 — so the near-v(0.05) set is the entire candidate list (median 12); predicted-ml spread within it is median 5.5 units (IQR 4.2-7.8, max 21.8) = ~1.1% of the 512 cap (3.1 within a 0.01 v-window). Nonzero, but the sibling head-quality audit measured ckpt5 marathon-regime ml accuracy at r=-0.03, MAE 126, bias -81, slope~0 — the sibling spread is below the head's demonstrated resolution; the grip is noise-level. (Q2 played-move test) the played squander move ranks mid-pack under v (mean 5.1/13, v-argmax only 25% vs 67% at controls) and U does NOT systematically demote it (mean rank 5.12 vs 5.12 at k=0.2; 10 worsen / 9 improve). Weak sign-consistent evidence the head perceives the dawdle: 42/64 (66%) of played squander moves were above-median predicted ml among near-v candidates (game-level mean 0.656, SE 0.074 across 8 games, p~0.07 clustered). (Q3 collateral) clean: conversion controls flip 0% at ALL k<=1.0 (min finite critical-k ~17); ungated midgame flips 0% up to k=0.5 and 8.3% (2/24) at k=1.0. (k-grid) squander flip rates: 4.7% @k=0.05-0.1, 12.5% @0.2 (4/8 games), 29.7% @0.5 (8/8 games), 54.7% @1.0; median critical-k 0.83; all flips reduce predicted ml; median v-cost of a flip 0.0004-0.0009; median predicted-ml gain on flip only 2.0-2.6 units (~0.5% of cap). POISONING FACTS that void the flips as validated improvements: (a) the v-gate orienting the utility is broken exactly where it must act — 'leader |v|>0.6' predicted the actual winner only 31/64 (48%, coin flip); the +-0.6 read is to-move parity optimism: all 26 positions whose successors pass the turn flip wholesale to ~ -v_base, while all 38 mid-chain (same-player) successors keep +v; (b) the ml head also carries a cross-move discontinuity (controls: ml_base 9.8 -> successor ml ~21, median +25 jump over one action), so only same-parity sibling comparisons are valid (they are: stm_next is uniform within every position probed); (c) zero terminal/immediate-win candidates appeared in any top-12+played set — no missed mate-in-1 for the utility to trivially fix. CONCLUSION: the squander problem is not 'v-ties a moves-left utility could break'; it is that BOTH v and ml are flat noise at marathon positions and even the win/lose sign needed to aim the utility is a coin flip there.
verdict: No k delivers VALIDATED dawdle discrimination with the current ckpt5 heads. Mechanically, k in [0.2, 0.5] meets the letter of the criterion — flips 12.5-29.7% of squander-point choices toward lower predicted moves-left while flipping 0% of healthy conversion controls (and 0% of ungated midgame choices at k<=0.5) at negligible v-cost (<0.001) — so the mechanism is SAFE and a KataGo-style utility at k~0.2-0.3 would not damage healthy play. But the flips cannot be certified as faster conversions: the leader designation the utility's sign depends on is 48% predictive (to-move parity optimism, not a real edge), and the per-sibling ml differences it acts on (~1% of cap) are below the head's measured marathon-regime resolution (r~0, MAE 126, near-constant output). At KataGo-conventional k (0.05-0.1) only ~5% of squander choices flip — nothing changes. Recommendation to carry into the design: do NOT wire the utility into search yet; it is gated on (1) fixing the moves_left head (currently near-constant; raise weight/recalibrate per the head-audit task, and resolve the plies-vs-decisions target unit ambiguity) and (2) mitigating the to-move +-0.6 parity optimism of the value head at long games, since the utility needs sign(v) as its rudder. Once a retrained head shows sibling-level resolution, k~0.2 (normalized-ml units) is the empirically safe starting weight, with the 0%-collateral margin re-verified.

key_numbers.leader_won_at_squander_points: 31/64 (48% — v>0.6 leader read is coin-flip predictive)
key_numbers.parity_flip_structure: 26/26 turn-passing successors read ~ -v_base; 38/38 mid-chain successors read ~ +v_base
key_numbers.head_marathon_accuracy_from_sibling_audi: r=-0.03, MAE 126, bias -81, slope ~0 (ckpt5 on m3ep9)

caveats: One-ply lookahead proxy, not a full MCTS backup: in real search the utility aggregates over subtrees and could behave differently; this probe measures only whether the immediate-move choice would change.

Squander sample is clustered: 64 positions = 8 per game x 8 games, all from main_3 epoch 9; game-level statistics reported where it matters (flips at k=0.2 hit 4/8 games, k=0.5 hit 8/8; dawdle-flag game-level SE 0.074).

Successor states evaluated immediately after one action may be mid-chain (Hexo multi-action turns) — off-distribution for the net. Within-position rankings are internally valid (stm_next uniform across candidates in all 79 positions), but absolute v/ml levels across the move are parity-contaminated (the documented FirstStone/to-move confound).

Head-unit ambiguity: npz moves_left targets observed in main_3 shards are plies-like (ml + turn_index = game length exactly, max 853 > cap), while current samples.py defines decisions-remaining; all flip/ranking results are unit-invariant (monotone decode), but absolute 'ml units' figures should not be read strictly as decisions.
ckpt5 ('healthy lens') is evaluating ep9 marathon positions outside its own self-play distribution; a stronger/later net could show more sibling v-separation at the same positions.

The corpus's squander events were mined with the same ckpt5 lens (|v|>0.6); given the 48% leader_won rate, some 'squander points' may not contain a genuine win to squander — this weakens the premise of Q2 but is itself a load-bearing finding.

Probe scripts and raw outputs were produced by a verified prior attempt of this task (sanity, replay-determinism cross-check vs corpus values, and decode-path audit all re-validated this session); the critical-k/parity analysis is new this session.
Control flip rate 0% has limited power at n=15 (upper 95% binomial bound ~18%); midgame n=24 adds support (0% at k<=0.5).
